clue.text: A meal favoured by some drivers, we hear

indicators.note: we hear tells us the words are judged by how they sound when spoken

parts.note: golfers hitting a driver off the tee may like the ball perched on a high tee

explanation.surface: A lorry drivers' café meal, perhaps, talked about over the counter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drivers' suggests motorists, but these are golfers, who tee the ball up high for a driver; said out loud, that tee matches the meal. HIGH TEA is a British early-evening cooked meal.
explanation.definitionFit: High tea is an early-evening British repast with hot food, eaten in place of a late dinner.

clue.text: Shakespearian war-cry !

parts.note: Mark Antony in Julius Caesar says Caesar's spirit will cry this word and let slip the dogs of war

explanation.definitionFit: In Julius Caesar the cry signalling general slaughter is this word for chaos and devastation.

clue.text: Flowers from an unnatural sun mirage

indicators.note: something unnatural is not as it normally is, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Blooms seen in an illusion caused by a strange sun.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unnatural' rearranges the letters of 'sun mirage'.
explanation.definitionFit: Geraniums are popular flowering garden and pot plants, also called pelargoniums.

clue.text: On the go, and geared for jam-making !

definitions.text: On the go, and geared for jam-making !

parts.words: On the go, and geared for jam-making !
parts.note: vehicles on the move, which bring the roads to a standstill when they jam

explanation.walkthrough: 'Jam-making' suggests fruit preserving, but the jam is a hold-up of cars on the roads.
explanation.definitionFit: Vehicles moving on the roads are what clog up into a jam.

clue.text: Part-time worker ?

parts.note: someone whose working time is spent playing roles, or parts

explanation.walkthrough: 'Part-time' reads as working reduced hours, but the worker spends all their time in parts, as a stage player.
explanation.definitionFit: A stage performer works by taking roles in plays.

clue.text: One in search of a shilling jumper ?

definitions.text: One in search of a shilling jumper ?

parts.note: s is the abbreviation for the old British shilling coin
a hopper is something that jumps

explanation.surface: Someone browsing the shops hoping for a cheap woolly sweater.
explanation.walkthrough: A shilling was an old British coin; 'jumper' reads as a sweater but is a hopper, an insect that jumps. The whole clue also describes someone out buying a cheap sweater.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone looking round stores for a bargain garment is a customer out buying.

clue.text: Browned off ? Not if the head is covered

definitions.text: Browned off ? Not if the head is covered

parts.words: Browned off ? Not if the head is covered
parts.note: skin darkened by strong rays, which a hat on the head would prevent

explanation.walkthrough: 'Browned off' is slang for fed up, but here it means literally tanned, which a hat would stop.
explanation.definitionFit: Skin scorched or tanned by too much sun is what a hat protects against.

clue.text: See 19

parts.note: this light is clued inside the clue at 19, as the partner word naming twists and bends in a lane

explanation.walkthrough: The clue at 19 plays on the proverb 'it's a long lane that has no turning': this light and that one together name a lane's turnings, the in-bends and out-bends.
explanation.definitionFit: The pair names a road's bends outward and inward, its turnings.

clue.text: Heady tea-maker ?

definitions.meaning: a poll is a head, so the word reads as having to do with a head
the nursery rhyme girl who puts the kettle on so we can all have tea

explanation.walkthrough: 'Polly put the kettle on' is the nursery rhyme; POLL is an old word for the head, so adding Y makes a mock adjective 'heady'.
explanation.definitionFit: The rhyme's girl boils the kettle for tea, and a poll is the scalp, so the name sounds like a head-adjective.

clue.text: Birds the communist forces from cover

parts.note: Red is a nickname for a communist
to start game is to flush it out of hiding

explanation.surface: Birds being driven out of hiding by a leftist militia.
explanation.walkthrough: To start an animal is the hunting term for driving it from cover.
explanation.definitionFit: Redstarts are small songbirds with a rust-coloured tail.

clue.text: It's not quite the same thing

definitions.text: It's not quite the same thing

parts.words: It's not quite the same thing
parts.note: a description of a slightly different version or form of something

explanation.definitionFit: A variant is an alternative form differing a little from the standard one.

clue.text: Irritated, through failure to grasp things properly ?

definitions.text: through failure to grasp things properly ?
definitions.meaning: a stinging plant hurts you if you touch it gingerly rather than grasping it firmly

explanation.walkthrough: The second reading draws on the saying that a stinging nettle grasped firmly does not sting; take hold timidly and you get stung.
explanation.definitionFit: Being annoyed is being stung in temper, and literally a nettle stings a hand that does not grip it boldly.

clue.text: Describing some that get needled with long-lasting leaves

definitions.text: Describing some that get needled with long-lasting leaves

parts.words: Describing some that get needled with long-lasting leaves
parts.note: an adjective for trees such as pines that bear needles and stay evergreen

explanation.walkthrough: 'Get needled' suggests being annoyed, but it means bearing needles, as pines and firs do.
explanation.definitionFit: Cone-bearing trees such as firs carry needle leaves that persist all year.

clue.text: Little island in river reaches they otherwise forget

indicators.note: forget tells us to drop the surrounding letters of these words and keep a run from inside them

explanation.surface: Advice to forget about a small river island in a different way.
explanation.walkthrough: Ignore the outer letters of 'they otherwise' and the run left straddling the two words gives the island. An EYOT (ait) is a small island in a river, common on the Thames.
explanation.definitionFit: An eyot is a small islet, especially one in a river such as the Thames.

clue.text: Very little change from French sources

indicators.note: from tells us the letters are taken out of the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: Barely any money comes back from French suppliers.
explanation.walkthrough: The run sits across the join of 'French sources'. A SOU was an old French coin of tiny value, so it fits 'very little change'.
explanation.definitionFit: A sou was a French coin worth very little, hence a tiny sum of money.

clue.text: Falsely pretended I must deal in turn

indicators.note: in turn suggests the letters take a turn, rearranged into another order

explanation.surface: I have to deal cards in turn, though I was only feigning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In turn' signals rearranging the letters of 'I must deal'.
explanation.definitionFit: Simulated means feigned, made to look real when it was not.

clue.text: Bed one plant, and up comes another !

definitions.note: the definition stands for another plant, a shrub

parts.note: a cot is a small bed
taken as written
an aster is a daisy-like garden plant

explanation.surface: A gardener beds in one plant and a different one springs up.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is 'another', meaning another plant: the pieces naming one plant combine to name a second, a shrub with red berries.
explanation.definitionFit: Cotoneaster is a berry-bearing garden shrub, so it is a further plant beyond the aster.

clue.text: Teasing hill guide ?

definitions.note: the definition is a verb form; the answer is the person doing the teasing

parts.note: a tor is a rocky hill, as on Dartmoor
a mentor is a trusted guide or adviser

explanation.surface: A mountain guide who likes to tease the climbers.
explanation.walkthrough: A TOR is a rocky hill or outcrop, typical of Dartmoor in south-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: A tormentor is one who teases or harasses another persistently.

clue.text: Lucky — at last!

parts.note: the saying that success comes on the third attempt, with the word lucky after it

explanation.walkthrough: The phrase completes the saying 'third time lucky', which hopes success comes at last on the third go.
explanation.definitionFit: Third time lucky is the saying that the third try will finally succeed.

clue.text: Square dames turn out for these in fancy dress

indicators.note: turn out suggests rearranging, so these letters come out in a new order

explanation.surface: Ladies from a square dance show up in costume.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turn out' reads as attending, but it rearranges the letters of 'Square dames'.
explanation.definitionFit: Masquerades are disguises or costumed balls, the occasions and outfits of fancy dress.

clue.text: Seeks a net profit at the seaside

definitions.text: Seeks a net profit at the seaside

parts.words: Seeks a net profit at the seaside
parts.note: fishes with a hand net for small crustaceans along the beach

explanation.walkthrough: 'Net profit' reads as business earnings, but it is a catch made with a net on the shore.
explanation.definitionFit: To shrimp is to fish for small crustaceans, often with a net at the shoreline.

clue.text: It's a long lane that has no these and 6

definitions.text: It's a long lane that has no these and 6

parts.words: It's a long lane that has no these and 6
parts.note: the proverb says a long lane has no turning; the twists in and out of a lane are its turnings

explanation.walkthrough: The proverb 'it's a long lane that has no turning' is bent so that the turnings become this answer and that of 6, which together form the phrase for twists and details.
explanation.definitionFit: The pair names the bends a road makes inward and outward, its turnings.

clue.text: This rates tears, though it's decorative

definitions.text: This rates tears, though it's decorative

parts.words: This rates tears, though it's decorative
parts.note: a fabric whose pattern is made of holes, which would count as rips in any other cloth

explanation.walkthrough: 'Tears' reads as weeping, but here means rips: this fabric is all holes yet ornamental.
explanation.definitionFit: Lace is an openwork fabric of holes used as ornamental trimming.

clue.text: Became close, so many took a breather

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, so many
a lung is the organ we breathe with

explanation.surface: Things got intimate, so a crowd stepped out for some air.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Took a breather' suggests a rest; the breather is a lung.
explanation.definitionFit: To have clung is to have held on tightly or stayed near.

clue.text: Apple-guarding sisters

parts.note: the nymphs of Greek myth who tended a tree bearing golden apples

explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth these nymphs kept the garden of Hera's golden apples, which Heracles had to steal.

clue.text: Edgy sort of topic

definitions.note: the definition is an adjective; the answer is a small loop used as an edge

indicators.note: sort of hints at sorting the letters, putting them in a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A subject that is somewhat nervy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Edgy' reads as tense, but it means used on edges: a PICOT is a small loop forming a decorative border on lace or ribbon.
explanation.definitionFit: A picot is a tiny ornamental loop worked along the border of fabric.

clue.text: Taken by those who would rise in the household

definitions.text: Taken by those who would rise in the household

parts.words: Taken by those who would rise in the household
parts.note: climbing upstairs in a house, or taking measures to get on

explanation.walkthrough: Climbing to an upper floor takes these, and so does advancing one's position.
explanation.definitionFit: Stairs are climbed one at a time, and one takes measures to advance.

clue.text: I'm backing the French, in the long run !

indicators.note: backing means the two letters of I'm are read backwards

parts.note: le is French for the

explanation.surface: Getting behind the French over the long term.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Backing' looks like support or wagering, but it is the reversal signal; 'long run' is the definition, a distance race.
explanation.definitionFit: A mile is a long distance race or run, as in the four-minute mile.

clue.text: Traveller carries his own trophy round our little island

indicators.note: round means the trophy letters go about the other pieces

parts.note: TT stands for ... Trophy, the Isle of Man motorcycle races, so it is this traveller's own trophy
taken as written
IS is a short form of island

explanation.surface: A traveller hauls a prize around a small British island.
explanation.walkthrough: The TT (Tourist Trophy) is the motorcycle race on the Isle of Man, hence 'his own trophy' for a traveller of this kind.
explanation.definitionFit: A tourist is someone travelling for pleasure, a holidaying visitor.

clue.text: Big business for the harvester

definitions.meaning: a large commercial group formed by merging firms
a farm machine that both reaps and threshes grain

explanation.surface: A large firm in the business of harvesting.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a merged commercial association and a reaping-threshing machine on a farm.

clue.text: Leafy corner for a pet's attention ?

parts.note: a dog is a familiar pet, here possessive
to give ear is to give attention

explanation.surface: A cosy leafy spot where a pet gets noticed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leafy' suggests a garden nook, but it means a page of a book: a turned-down corner of a leaf.
explanation.definitionFit: A turned-down corner of a book's page is named after a hound's floppy lug.

clue.text: Decorations for top college squares

parts.note: the mortarboard, a square academic cap, has a hanging ornament on its top

explanation.walkthrough: 'College squares' reads as quadrangles, but these squares are mortarboards, the flat square caps worn at graduation.
explanation.definitionFit: A mortarboard has a hanging tuft of threads as its ornament.
